title: Satisfiability of a recursively filled clause chain
statement: Let $n\ge 0$. A literal on $n$ coordinates specifies an index and a required sign; an assignment satisfies it when its value at that index is the required sign. Suppose the indices in each of two lists of literals are pairwise distinct, the two lists use disjoint sets of indices, and an initial assignment satisfies at least one literal in the first list. Recursively fill the auxiliary coordinates by the stated rule: at each step, set the auxiliary coordinate according to whether either of the first two current literals is satisfied. The resulting assignment satisfies at least one literal in every clause of the recursively constructed chain.
hypotheses_covered: indices in the first literal list are pairwise distinct
indices in the auxiliary list are pairwise distinct
the two lists have disjoint index sets
the initial assignment satisfies at least one literal in the first list
